A1.justification: Both complete 20-page PDFs describe the same TreeLoRA study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TreeLoRA experiments on vision transformers and language models, including performance, forgetting, runtime, ablations, and additional evaluations in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix A. Retaining results from v1 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3, Equations (1)–(3), and Algorithm 1 retain the same gradient-similarity tree, LCB search, and sparse adapter updates. The added explanation of reduced dimensionality does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Split CIFAR-100, Split ImageNet-R, Split CUB-200, TRACE, Math-LLM, and the additional task sequences in Appendix A.6. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in corresponding experiments, including InfLoRA in Table 11 and SAPT and TASL in Table 12. The changed SAPT citation suffix does not represent a different comparison method.

E3.justification: The versions retain the same splits, preprocessing, metrics, training budgets, model configurations, task orders, and SAPT replay exclusion. Appendix A.3 corrects the LLM implementation heading without revising the reported settings.

E4.justification: The epoch and depth analyses, component ablation, hyperparameter sensitivity study, task-order tests, and tree visualizations remain unchanged in Tables 2, 4–6, and 10 and Figures 5 and 8. No supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same three-run averaging and standard-deviation reporting, including Tables 1, 3, 6, and 7 and Figures 4, 6, and 7. No run counts, seed information, or statistical procedures change.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, TreeLoRA retains 88.54 ± 0.05% accuracy in Table 1, 54.77 ± 1.1% Mistral overall performance in Table 3, and 47.13% overall performance in Table 13.

T1.justification: Assumption 1, Theorem 1, Lemma 1, and the Appendix C proofs remain unchanged. Section 3.2 explains that the existing d' denotes reduced dimensionality, without changing the estimator, introducing a new theoretical assumption, or revising mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: hierarchical adapter sharing, efficient bandit search, sparse updates, and tighter regret bounds. The claimed speedups remain up to 3.2 times for ViTs and 2.4 times for LLMs.

C2.justification: The explanations of knowledge sharing, efficiency, applicability, and the future challenge of time-varying task relationships remain unchanged. Section 3.1 rephrases the shared-versus-task-specific layer description without introducing a substantive new interpretation or limitation.

D1.justification: The implementation information in Section 3.3 and Appendix A.3, hardware specifications, hyperparameters, resource requirements, and code/data access statement remain unchanged. Correcting the LLM heading adds no reproducibility details.

R1.justification: AdaLoRA changes attribution from Hu et al. (2024) to Zhang et al. (2023a), and GaLore from Lin et al. (2023) to Zhao et al. (2024a). Their matching titles and descriptions identify the same works; these are bibliographic revisions without changes to research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 clarifies d' in Section 3.2, lightly rewrites the layer description and Appendix A.5 introduction, fixes the Appendix A.3 heading, revises citation metadata, and adds a JSPS funding acknowledgment. The section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Edited paragraphs and bibliography entries cause limited text reflow, particularly across reference pages 10–12. Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–13 retain their displays, captions, and placement; there is no visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 explains the previously unexplained reduced-dimension symbol in Section 3.2 and corrects the misleading LLM implementation heading in Appendix A.3. These changes modestly improve clarity. The methods, empirical evidence, and theoretical analysis remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
